international.title: Burnham’s devolution plans risk ‘significant disparities’ for people in England, MPs say – UK politics live
international.summary: Public accounts committee warns of ‘disparities in opportunities and outcomes’ depending on the type of strategic authority where people live Millions of British households will face annual energy bills of more than £2,000 a year for the first time since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as the cap on energy bills climbs for a third straight quarter, Jillian Ambrose reports. Commenting on the increase for the Conservatives, Andrew Bowie , the shadow energy secretary, said: It is an outrage that, as bills soar, Labour are not only piling green levies and taxes on to bills but signing us up to an EU scheme that risks pushing them even higher. Labour are utterly out of touch and could fix this tomorrow if they had the backbone. Right now, millions of families feel completely powerless in the face of reckless wars driving up energy prices, and they are being left to fend for themselves while bills spiral out of control. The meagre and poorly targeted support the government has promised will be wiped out by this rise, and many of those who most desperately need help won’t get a penny. The government needs to wake up to the scale of this crisis. Labour and the Tories net zero obsession is going to bankrupt Britain. We’re paying the price for Trump’s war in Iran & our failure to get off the fossil fuel rollercoaster coaster The UK supported that war, with US bombers launching from here It doesn’t have to be like this. We could transform our economy to be entirely based on clean, affordable energy. And we could ban the US from using our bases for good, and end our tacit support for their wars of aggression.
